nodes.description: PAK1 couples RAC1 and CDC42 to actin reorganization. Patient fibroblasts spread with an excess of filopodia, and the ATP-competitive PAK1 inhibitor FRAX486 fully reversed this, tying the cellular phenotype to PAK1 kinase activity. In neurons, PAK1 activation shapes the actin dynamics of neurite outgrowth, and a PAK1-LIMK1-cofilin route has been proposed; neither has been measured with patient alleles in neurons.

nodes.description: Resting PAK1 is a trans-inhibited homodimer in which the autoinhibitory switch domain of each monomer covers the kinase domain of the other; RAC1 or CDC42 binding dissociates the dimer and activates the kinase. Disease variants sit in the N-terminal regulatory region (Thr84 in the GTPase binding region; Ser110, Pro121, Tyr131, Asn132, Ser133 and the Met143 hotspot) or in the kinase domain at its contact surface with the inhibitory switch (Tyr429, Leu470). Reduced dimerization was measured for Tyr131Cys and Tyr429Cys; for the other variants it is inferred from structural modelling.
